evidence.engine: Pinned DynamoDB Local 3.3.1: six records from four puts, one conditional update and one committed transaction; rejected conditional/transaction writes emit no records. Reopening retains stream, shard, event IDs, sequence numbers and images. Disable retains the table's latest stream identity. Backend table responses are not an AWS oracle: their identities bind the native records, while the live-AWS audit source governs table response semantics.
evidence.audit: AWS capture: ordered INSERT/MODIFY/REMOVE images, batch/transaction/PartiQL writes, enabled-view-change rejection, disable/reenable generation rotation, KEYS_ONLY records, unchanged old records after disabled writes, and DescribeStream after DeleteTable.
evidence.normalization: AWS shard topology is deployment-specific: collect all shards and compare records by key, preserving each key's captured order. Record IDs and sequence numbers are bound, not copied. Engine's single-shard identity is checked across reopen. Creation timestamps are not compared; local region is relocated and stream list order is not asserted.
evidence.excluded: No captured IAM denial or iterator-principal experiment, TTL deletion, expiry, post-DeleteTable GetRecords, or arbitrary iterator boundary expectations are inferred. Reopen reconstructs stackd services and SQLite handles over the retained native database.
